races.name: EMS Copiers Irish EBF Fillies Maiden
Irish Stallion Farms EBF Race

runners_data.name: Howd'yadoit
runners_data.note: Gary Carroll in the saddle for G M Lyons who is in good current form (8/17 over 14 days); Howd'yadoit's sole win came over this exact 5f trip on Good at Naas, she sits prominent and will press Keke throughout, making her the most natural beneficiary if Keke fades.

runners_data.name: Keke
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter here — W J Lee will look to slot straight to the front and control the tempo over 5f on Good turf, a surface and trip on which she has the best recent form record in the field (12/15 similar-going runs); Edward Lynam's runner carries blinkers and will be hardest to pass if not pressed hard early.

runners_data.name: Likedbymike
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes over for M J Byrne just six days after her last run; she has a strong recent placed record over this exact 5f/Good combination (three of last five runs placed) but has not won from a hold-up position in a small field, and her reliance on a strong pace is the key vulnerability today.

runners_data.name: Cardiff By The Sea
runners_data.note: J A Stack has had two winners from six runners in the past fortnight, and Cardiff By The Sea's sole win came over 5f on Soft, raising a mild query about whether Good ground is quite her optimum; she ran 14th last time on Good and must bounce back sharply, racing from a hold-up position that becomes harder to execute in a small field.

runners_data.name: Xerling
runners_data.note: Miss Natalia Lupini's lightly-raced three-year-old has placed twice in five runs and won over this exact 5f/Good combination, showing genuine raw ability; however, her truest role is at the rear of the field — Donagh O'Connor will struggle to find a true hold-up position in a field this small, and her style fit here is the weakest of the five runners despite the map placing her in midfield.

races.paceDynamic: Keke is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only five runners over 5f at Naas on Good turf, she is highly likely to slot straight to the lead unopposed — Howd'yadoit will press from a prominent position but neither horse is likely to push into a destructive battle. That creates a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front, which in a small field on Good ground at this trip rewards horses who can sit close to the pace and punch off it rather than those hunting them down from a true hold-up position. Likedbymike, Cardiff By The Sea, and Xerling are all hold-up or rear-of-field types, but the field's shape means genuine closers will need either a strong pace or a clear gap late — neither is guaranteed here. This race shape strongly favours the prominent and front-running profile: horses who track Keke at close quarters will be best positioned when she kicks, while true hold-up runners face an unfavourable geometry in a small, slowly-run field. The field contains more hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Likedbymike and Cardiff By The Sea are the most likely to push forward from their natural position, with Xerling, the truest hold-up type, least likely to secure her preferred spot despite being redistributed to midfield on the map.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Keke Controls, Front Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Keke dictates an uncontested lead and Howd'yadoit tracks her throughout, the pair race clear of the field.
scenarios.body: If Keke dictates an uncontested lead and Howd'yadoit tracks her throughout, the pair race clear of the field.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected and the front pair fade inside the final furlong, a closer gets a clear run.
scenarios.body: If the pace is stronger than expected and the front pair fade inside the final furlong, a closer gets a clear run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Howd'yadoit Overcomes Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Howd'yadoit travels better than Keke mid-race and takes it up before the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Howd'yadoit travels better than Keke mid-race and takes it up before the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Xerling Defies Race Shape
scenarios.trigger: If Xerling secures a midfield position naturally and the pace collapses, allowing her to swoopfrom an unexpected angle.
scenarios.body: If Xerling secures a midfield position naturally and the pace collapses, allowing her to swoopfrom an unexpected angle.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Keke is pressed by Howd'yadoit in the first furlong — if Carroll sends Howd'yadoit straight at the leader, the pace could spike and open the race up for Likedbymike or Cardiff By The Sea late.

Likedbymike's six-day turnaround is unusually quick; watch for any signs of freshness or reluctance in the stalls that could cost her a clean break, which would be fatal to a hold-up horse in a five-runner field.

Cardiff By The Sea's form reversal is required after a 14th on Good ground last time — watch whether Gavin Ryan pushes her forward from her natural hold-up position, effectively changing her race shape to give her a better chance.

Xerling's redistribution from true hold-up to mapped midfield means Donagh O'Connor may try to slot her closer than her natural style; watch the first two furlongs to see if the small field bunches in a way that accidentally hands her a better position than expected.

With only five runners on Good turf over 5f, the field is likely to compress into a tight group early — watch for Howd'yadoit's positioning at the break, as a sluggish start would push her into hold-up territory and significantly alter the two-horse prominent shape the race is built around.

races.name: Coolmore Stud Blackbeard Tipperary Stakes (Listed)

runners_data.name: Abletai
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who was placed on good ground over 5f on the most recent start; Grassick stable has no runners in the 14-day window suggesting this is a deliberate peaking run after 56 days off, but generating momentum from the back on a flat five furlongs is a significant ask.|

runners_data.name: Carry The Flag
runners_data.note: A P O'Brien second string but a course-and-distance winner on good ground who ran second most recently at Group level; prominent style with Ronan Whelan who rides the rail brilliantly, and the 14-day turnaround (8 from 43) shows the yard is firing.|

runners_data.name: Hanney Boy
runners_data.note: Consistent placed-only sprinter from a quiet yard (0 from 2 in 14 days) whose prominence style will draw him into the early position battle; has yet to win on good ground and steps sharply up in class from his last three efforts.|

runners_data.name: Rejoinder
runners_data.note: No form string available and no last-run data — complete unknown on pace angle and going preference; trainer De Aguiar has one runner from 14 entries recently, and the absence of race history makes this a genuine wildcard at Listed level.|

runners_data.name: Arrowstock
runners_data.note: Ran sixth on this course over 5f on good ground on debut, the only piece of evidence available; style unknown, lightly raced flag signals raw upside but also vulnerability, and the yard has had one runner from nine in the past fortnight.|

runners_data.name: Belle Island
runners_data.note: Hold-up style on a flat sprint track is a structural disadvantage; 76 days off the track since finishing sixth on soft, and her two placed efforts came on standard going at a different venue — returning against Listed company off this absence raises questions.|

runners_data.name: Big Negotiator
runners_data.note: The confirmed and uncontested front-runner of this field with a win and three places from four starts on good ground at Naas over 5f; Pat Twomey's horse wore a hood last time and goes again quickly (17 days), suggesting a trainer confident in his condition.|

runners_data.name: Brazilian Diva
runners_data.note: Won on good ground over 5f most recently and is on a very quick turnaround (10 days); prominent style will put her into the early scrimmage and Diego Lima will need to find a clean passage if the four-way battle for position heats up.|

runners_data.name: Celestial Crown
runners_data.note: Two runs only, with a useful second on soft ground over 5f and a seventh on good at this course; Ben Coen's stable (JP Murtagh, 3 from 22 in 14 days) is active and connected, and her unknown pace style leaves tactical options open.|

runners_data.name: Matriarchal
runners_data.note: Has won once on good ground over 5f and placed again on the same surface; Josh Halley's yard has been active and the 35-day gap is workable, but she has to find improvement at Listed level and the prominent position she needs is already crowded.|

races.paceDynamic: Big Negotiator is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with W J Lee in the saddle and a recent course win over this identical trip, he is highly likely to stride into an uncontested lead from the gates on this flat Naas five furlongs. Behind him, Carry The Flag, Hanney Boy, Brazilian Diva, and Matriarchal all want prominent positions, creating a congested battle for the next two or three berths that could cause interference or force some of those four wider or later than ideal between the two-furlong and three-furlong poles. Abletai and Belle Island sit deepest on the map, with Rejoinder, Arrowstock, and Celestial Crown all unknown quantities in terms of race positioning. With a single pace-setter dictating a sustainable rather than scorching fractions on good ground, this race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently just off the leader and produce a clean turn of foot in the final furlong, with hold-up horses facing the additional burden of threading through a bunched mid-race group.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Big Negotiator Controls Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Big Negotiator secures an uncontested lead and rations the fractions on good ground to suit a strong finishing kick.
scenarios.body: If Big Negotiator secures an uncontested lead and rations the fractions on good ground to suit a strong finishing kick.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Closer Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early battle for position between Carry The Flag, Hanney Boy, Brazilian Diva, and Matriarchal results in a faster-than-expected tempo that drains Big Negotiator.
scenarios.body: If the early battle for position between Carry The Flag, Hanney Boy, Brazilian Diva, and Matriarchal results in a faster-than-expected tempo that drains Big Negotiator.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Lightly Raced Type Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If one of Celestial Crown, Rejoinder, or Arrowstock is significantly ahead of their bare form figures and produces an unexpected performance from an untested angle.
scenarios.body: If one of Celestial Crown, Rejoinder, or Arrowstock is significantly ahead of their bare form figures and produces an unexpected performance from an untested angle.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong throughout and the hold-up horses Abletai and Belle Island find an unusually clear passage through the final furlong on a flat course.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely strong throughout and the hold-up horses Abletai and Belle Island find an unusually clear passage through the final furlong on a flat course.

watchPoints.text: Big Negotiator (W J Lee) must be watched from the gates — if he jumps cleanly and crosses to the rail immediately he controls the race; if he misses the break he loses his entire tactical advantage and the race dynamic changes completely.

The four-way battle for prominent position between Carry The Flag, Hanney Boy, Brazilian Diva, and Matriarchal is the single biggest tactical flashpoint — watch the first two furlongs for bumping, checking, or wide running that could compromise one or more of these at a critical stage.

Rejoinder's complete absence of public form data means any price-sensitive market move before post time warrants attention — if the market shortens significantly it implies stable confidence in a horse whose race shape is entirely unknown.

Abletai's 56-day absence and hold-up style on a flat five furlongs combine as a compounding concern — watch whether McCullagh is able to slot in closer than usual or whether he is anchored at the back with little room to manoeuvre late.

Belle Island has had 76 days off the track and returns in Listed company for the De Aguiar yard that also runs Rejoinder — watch whether she is ridden to make the most of what should be a truly-run race or whether she is given an educational spin.

races.name: Lawlor's Of Naas Supporting Naas GAA Senior Football Race Day Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Arctic Steps
runners_data.note: Strong sim-going record (2 wins, 3 places from 15 Good/Standard runs), returned to form with a win last time out over this course and trip 39 days ago, wears a hood, and races from hold-up position — should get a clear view from off the pace if the pace is genuine enough.

runners_data.name: Harry's Hill
runners_data.note: Veteran 8-year-old with a modest recent string (-67060) and a concerning 12/15 sim-going record; 6 days since last run and a 7lb claimer up, but has struggled to land a blow in similar fields and is up against it here.

runners_data.name: Lethimfly
runners_data.note: Noel Meade runner wearing a blindfold, drops back from 5f runs where he has placed (2nd, 3rd) on Standard ground; sim-going on Good is suspect (10/13), but recent form shows enough to suggest he remains competitive at this level if pace conditions suit.

runners_data.name: Sovereign Cry
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner in the field and gets a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.94, meaning today's prominent role is slightly out of character — however, the single win on this card came over 5f on Standard, and with no pressure likely the lead should be his; the STYLE_FIT caveat should temper enthusiasm.

runners_data.name: White Smoke
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly with best form over 5-6f on Good, placed at 5f/Good last time; 56 days off and a 7lb claimer adds risk, but the Good going and trip are positive boxes ticked.

runners_data.name: Bold Optimist
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with two wins and three places from 15 sim-going runs — those came predominantly on Standard rather than Good; 106 days since last run is the key concern, and while naturally a hold-up horse, the congestion in this field means he is unlikely to get the trailing position he needs.

runners_data.name: Nouvel Espoir
runners_data.note: Recent win on Soft (1/5f/SOF) gives a form boost, and the string reads 023641 showing progressive consistency; though a genuine hold-up type at heart, the overcrowded rear means he's likely to end up travelling closer to the pace than ideal — not necessarily a disadvantage at 5f if the pace is strong.

runners_data.name: Ardadslosttheplot
runners_data.note: Two-year-old (sic — 133lbs, shortest in the field) returning from 277 days off with only four career runs, all at 6-7f on Good or Soft; stepping down to 5f for the first time is an unknown, and the lengthy absence is a significant negative regardless of style fit.

runners_data.name: Cactus
runners_data.note: Trained by A.P. O'Brien whose yard is in form (T14: 7/31), and showed a placed effort at 5f/Good; however, six runs without a win and five finishing towards the rear on Good ground means the market will do the talking — the in-form stable is the only real hook.

runners_data.name: Jordan Breeze
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with a recent win on Soft (1/5f/SOF), two further places on Soft/Standard, and a handy 4lb claimer; Good ground is less proven (11/5f/GOO in the books), and the worry is that the front-end position is where he must be — if Sovereign Cry dictates, Jordan Breeze needs to go with him.

runners_data.name: Billboa
runners_data.note: Weathered 6-year-old whose sim-going record on turf is poor (1/15 on Good/Standard), with most career form on Standard; no notable yard activity (T14: 0/0) and no clear angle to recommend him today.

runners_data.name: Tawaazon
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old whose recent 2/5f/GOO and 4/6f/GOO show he can place on this going; 3 days since last run (very quick turnaround) and wears a hood and blindfold combination — hold-up type who benefits from a strong early pace but may find too many between him and daylight in a 13-runner field.

runners_data.name: Phil's Dream
runners_data.note: Lowest-rated runner in the field (OR=49) but wears three pieces of headgear (hood, tongue tie, visor), and McConnell's yard had a winner 14 days ago; a 5f/Good profile shows poor sim-going form (2/15), and this is a tough assignment off the bottom weight.

races.paceDynamic: Sovereign Cry is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 13-runner field and, with no genuine pace rival likely to seriously contest the early lead, should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over this flat Naas 5f on Good ground. Jordan Breeze is the only other prominent-style runner and will push for a position close to the pace, but neither is likely to generate the sort of pressured, searingly fast early fractions that would blow the race wide open for closers. The bulk of this field — Arctic Steps, Harry's Hill, Lethimfly, White Smoke, Nouvel Espoir, Cactus, Ardadslosttheplot, Bold Optimist, Billboa, Tawaazon, and Phil's Dream — are true hold-up types, but the field holds far more hold-up runners than the race can accommodate at the rear, and Nouvel Espoir, Cactus, and Ardadslosttheplot are the most likely to be pushed forward out of role by the congestion. With Sovereign Cry controlling an uncontested lead at a measured pace and little genuine front-end pressure, this race shape most favours horses racing prominently or with early position who can travel comfortably just off the pace and pounce in the final furlong — patient hold-up finishers launching from deep will need either a strong pace or a clear run that this race shape is unlikely to guarantee.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sovereign Cry Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Sovereign Cry bowls along unchallenged and sets a steady-to-fair gallop that suits Jordan Breeze to travel in behind.
scenarios.body: If Sovereign Cry bowls along unchallenged and sets a steady-to-fair gallop that suits Jordan Breeze to travel in behind.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fight It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Jordan Breeze pushes Sovereign Cry for the lead early and the two burn each other off, creating a genuinely honest pace.
scenarios.body: If Jordan Breeze pushes Sovereign Cry for the lead early and the two burn each other off, creating a genuinely honest pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Sovereign Cry's pace is fast enough and a clear run materialises down the outside for a hold-up runner from the middle of the field.
scenarios.body: If Sovereign Cry's pace is fast enough and a clear run materialises down the outside for a hold-up runner from the middle of the field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If the opening fractions are unusually slow and the entire field swarms into a bunch entering the final 2f, turning it into a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: If the opening fractions are unusually slow and the entire field swarms into a bunch entering the final 2f, turning it into a sprint finish.

watchPoints.text: Sovereign Cry's ability to get away cleanly at the start is critical — if he stumbles or is slow into stride, the entire race shape collapses and the field bunches immediately, wiping out his positional advantage.

Jordan Breeze's jockey (Robyn Donaghue-Leahy, 4lb claimer) must decide very quickly whether to contest the lead or settle in behind — if she fires Jordan Breeze at Sovereign Cry early, the gallop accelerates and opens the race for hold-up types.

The overcrowded hold-up group creates significant traffic risk in the final 2f — watch Arctic Steps and Tawaazon in particular, as both need a clear passage that may not come in a 13-runner sprint field.

Cactus (A.P. O'Brien, T14: 7/31) and Nouvel Espoir (recent winner, consistent form) are the two redistributed horses most likely to push forward ahead of their natural role — if either secures an unexpected prominent position, they become dangers the market may have underestimated.

Ardadslosttheplot returns from 277 days off and steps down in trip; watch the market in the final 30 minutes — any significant market move from a big price could signal stable confidence that the layoff has not blunted ability.

races.name: Care At Home Handicap (0-60)

runners_data.name: Chapel Island
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist for A Oliver who fades in the finish; 14 days since last run and similar-going form shows 0 wins and 0 places in 7 attempts, making this a tough ask at 10f+ on good turf.|

runners_data.name: Connecteo
runners_data.note: Redistributed onto the lead from a true hold-up role; A Oliver yard in 1-from-8 form over 14 days, STYLE_FIT of 0.80 is the biggest discount in the field, but uncontested lead at a crawl is a genuine live scenario if rivals are slow to react.|

runners_data.name: Rodeo Blues
runners_data.note: Strong profile for this race — won at 10f on good ground in recent form (1/10f/GOO), trained by Joseph O'Brien with T14 of 10/67, ridden by Dylan Browne McMonagle; best-credentialled runner on paper and the trip and going suit perfectly.|

runners_data.name: The Holy Apostle
runners_data.note: Brendan Duke-trained hold-up type with a hood, last seen finishing ninth at 10f on soft; has placed at 7f on soft but the combination of good ground and 1m3f is an unknown, and 0 wins in 9 similar-going starts tempers optimism.|

runners_data.name: Captain Con
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner for Noel Meade who fades late; 29 days between runs and consistently finishes mid-to-rear in similar-going handicaps, with 0 wins and 0 places from 5 such efforts — needs something to go wrong for others.|

runners_data.name: Point Cartwright
runners_data.note: Finished second at 12f on good last time, which is the standout recent placing in this field; Adrian McGuinness has 1 from 27 over 14 days and the fade-in-finish flag is a concern, but the longer trip is clearly suiting him.|

runners_data.name: Maker's Mark
runners_data.note: True hold-up type shuffled to midfield on the map (STYLE_FIT 0.91); amateur rider Sadhbh Tormey claims 7lbs, form figures show 0 wins and 0 places from 8 similar-going starts, and fades in finishes — combination of factors makes this hard to recommend.|

runners_data.name: Nephin Mountain
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse placed in midfield by redistribution (STYLE_FIT 0.90); Declan McDonogh is a positive booking and the horse has placed four times in recent form including a 4th at 9f on good, suggesting ability — distance step up is the key question.|

runners_data.name: Private Larry
runners_data.note: Consistent finisher in the 8-10th range across every run, with all career form pointing firmly to the rear division; naturally a hold-up horse pushed to midfield (STYLE_FIT 0.90) and the fade flag compounds the problem — Leigh Roche will need a big ride.|

runners_data.name: Millhone
runners_data.note: Wears a hood (hg:p) and is a true hold-up type mapped to midfield by necessity (STYLE_FIT 0.90); Charles Weld-trained, last ran 16 days ago with a best finish of 7th at 8f on good — the step to 1m3f is uncharted territory.|

runners_data.name: Wingit
runners_data.note: Long 155-day absence is the defining factor here; Gavin Cromwell sends it out with STYLE_FIT 0.90 in a 19-runner field, all career form is on standard ground at 7-8f on Tapeta at Dundalk — this trip and going combination is completely new.|

runners_data.name: Six Wings
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with hood and tongue-tie, trained by Paul Flynn (T14 3/23); all four career starts have been on good ground with placings of 6th, 7th and 9th — the 0-from-4 good-ground record suggests the surface is not the issue but ability might be.|

runners_data.name: Darwin's Angel
runners_data.note: Wears a visor (hg:v) and ran 57 days ago, a notable absence for a handicapper; true hold-up type (STYLE_FIT 0.90) with a best of 6th in 11 similar-going attempts — the visor change could signal a stable that's working to find an angle.|

runners_data.name: Cadreville
runners_data.note: Last-time-out third at 10f on good is the best recent piece of form among the redistributed midfielders; Neve Bennett claims 7lbs and the Fahey yard has 0 from 5 over 14 days, but the form is live enough to keep onside.|

runners_data.name: Canon Law
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Brendan Duke (same trainer as The Holy Apostle) placed in midfield by redistribution (STYLE_FIT 0.93); ran 12 days ago, best finish is a 5th at 7f on heavy, and the good ground at 1m3f looks completely against its grain.|

runners_data.name: Jewels Legacy
runners_data.note: Wears blinkers (hg:b) and has finished 9th, 10th, 6th, 9th and 13th in five good-ground runs — the blinkers are clearly not unlocking anything; STYLE_FIT 0.92 and all fade flags active, this would need an exceptional trip through the field.|

runners_data.name: Swift Charm
runners_data.note: Two consecutive third-place finishes at 10f on good (3/10f/GOO twice) give this horse the best recent-run consistency in the redistributed group; hood and tongue-tie worn, W R Crawford yard — the trip is proven and the form is trending in the right direction.|

runners_data.name: Flagstone Lady
runners_data.note: No jockey listed which is a live concern in a 19-runner field; true hold-up type pushed to midfield (STYLE_FIT 0.90) with a fade flag, and all four starts show double-figure or near-double-figure finishes on good ground — hard to make a case.|

runners_data.name: Music And Song
runners_data.note: Hood worn (hg:p) and trained by Thomas Dowling (T14 0/1); form figures include a 4th at 10f on good which gives some hope at the trip, but four of five runs show single-figure-teen or 9th-place finishes — no jockey listed adds further uncertainty.|

races.paceDynamic: Connecteo is the only confirmed front-runner in this 19-runner 1m3f handicap and, despite being a redistributed hold-up type pushed onto the lead by necessity, will set a sustainable, uncontested pace on good ground at Naas — creating a controlled, single-file tempo that will not string the field out early. With no genuine pace rival pressing Connecteo through the opening furlongs, the fractions are likely to be measured, preserving a strong gallop into the straight but avoiding the kind of brutal early burn that would shred stayers. The majority of the field are true hold-up horses compressed into the midfield on the map, meaning the race will be tightly bunched through the middle stages and the decisive move will come from off the pace in the final two furlongs. This shape — a lone, uncontested, moderate gallop followed by a sustained home-straight drive — strongly favours horses with genuine stamina, a turn of foot off a steady pace, and the ability to travel through traffic, making the classic front-to-midfield stalker or strong-finishing stayer the profile to beat. The field holds far more hold-up types than the pace map can physically accommodate at the rear; Flagstone Lady, Private Larry, Nephin Mountain and Millhone are genuine prominent or hold-up types who are unlikely to secure their natural position in a 19-runner field, with Rodeo Blues and Swift Charm — both carrying strong recent form at the trip — best placed to capitalise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Stayer Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Connecteo dictates a steady, uncontested gallop and the field remains bunched until the straight, releasing a stamina-sapping sustained drive.
scenarios.body: If Connecteo dictates a steady, uncontested gallop and the field remains bunched until the straight, releasing a stamina-sapping sustained drive.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Traffic Trouble, Wide Run Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the large field causes significant congestion in the straight, forcing several hold-up horses wide and giving an advantage to those who find a clear run.
scenarios.body: If the large field causes significant congestion in the straight, forcing several hold-up horses wide and giving an advantage to those who find a clear run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Connecteo, racing on the lead from redistribution, finds the uncontested fractions so comfortable that it builds an unassailable advantage before the closing stages begin.
scenarios.body: If Connecteo, racing on the lead from redistribution, finds the uncontested fractions so comfortable that it builds an unassailable advantage before the closing stages begin.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is quick enough to tire the leaders and the hold-up horses genuinely get a clear run through the field in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If the tempo is quick enough to tire the leaders and the hold-up horses genuinely get a clear run through the field in the final furlong.

watchPoints.text: Rodeo Blues is the one runner with a recent win at 10f on good ground, a top jockey booking (Dylan Browne McMonagle) and a trainer (Joseph O'Brien) firing at a 10/67 strike rate — watch it as the most likely beneficiary of the controlled pace scenario.

With 19 runners over 1m3f at Naas, traffic congestion in the straight is a serious risk; any hold-up horse caught on the inner — particularly Nephin Mountain, Private Larry or Darwin's Angel — could find the run coming too late if the field fans wide.

Connecteo's redistribution onto the lead (STYLE_FIT 0.80) means its pace-setting role is unproven — if it drops back from the front early or fails to hold the position, the race loses its only pace anchor and the tactical picture becomes chaotic for a 19-runner field.

Swift Charm's back-to-back thirds at 10f on good give it more live recent form than most of its redistributed midfield companions — if it secures a clear run from the outside, it is the one horse in that group with the form to justify consideration.

Point Cartwright's second at 12f on good last time suggests the step beyond a mile is genuinely suiting it; the Ronan Whelan booking adds confidence, and a clean run from the rear could make it a dangerous each-way player if the pace collapses in the straight.

races.name: TRM Stay Cool Stay Sound Rated Race

runners_data.name: Suzie Songs
runners_data.note: The race-shaper here — she gets a clear lead under James Ryan for G M Lyons and her record on Good going (5/5 sim-going, two wins) is a concrete asset; the STYLE_FIT flag relates to her being rated as P rather than L, but in a field this light on true pace she will effectively function as the sole pace-setter.

runners_data.name: Yaupon De Replay
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes a strong hold-up type for Joseph O'Brien (13/63 T14), and the booking alone demands respect; his last run was 81 days ago, his form on Good going is limited to two outings, and he needs the pace to be truly honest over 7f for his late run to materialise.

runners_data.name: Frescobaldi
runners_data.note: Shane Foley partners a horse with genuine course-relevant experience — three runs at 7f including a win — and his naturally prominent style should allow him to track Suzie Songs cleanly without fighting for position the way the redistributed trio will; the step back from 6f trips in his last two runs makes 7f a comfortable fit.

runners_data.name: Ocean's Breath
runners_data.note: Won his most recent start over this exact trip and going (1/7f/GOO) and is clearly a live contender on form, but his natural urge to race prominently puts him in competition with Suzie Songs, Frescobaldi, and L L Koulsty for early berths — he may have to use more energy than ideal to secure a position that should come easily to him.

runners_data.name: L L Koulsty
runners_data.note: Rory Mulligan (5lb claim) takes a horse who has shown his best form at 6-7f on soft/heavy and whose sole Good-ground run (1/6 sim-going) yielded nothing; pushed into midfield on this map because the field is awash with prominent types, he has the lowest style-fit score and is fighting conditions, a trip stretch, and a positional disadvantage all at once.

runners_data.name: Sir Benji
runners_data.note: Interesting profile — both career runs have been over 10f on Good and Heavy, so dropping to 7f for Gavin Cromwell is a significant trip-shortening experiment; his natural prominent style will be difficult to express here and his class at this trip is unproven, making him the most speculative runner in the field despite a decent OR.

races.paceDynamic: Suzie Songs is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no other natural leader to press her, she should stride into an uncontested lead through the early stages of this 7f Naas contest on Good ground. The field behind her is stacked with genuine prominent types — Ocean's Breath, L L Koulsty, and Sir Benji all want to race close to the pace but cannot all do so, meaning at least two of them will be forced to sit in a position that doesn't suit their natural game. Yaupon De Replay and Frescobaldi complete the picture, the former a hold-up type who will need the race to set up for a late run, the latter naturally prominent but likely finding himself fighting for room in a congested mid-group. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate — of those redistributed, Ocean's Breath (recent winning form on Good, G M Lyons in form) looks most likely to actually secure a prominent berth alongside Suzie Songs. This race shape strongly favours Suzie Songs herself and any horse with the class and tactical flexibility to track a sustainable, uncontested pace before picking up in the final two furlongs — a controlled-tempo setup that rewards closers with a true turn of foot over those scrambling from an unnatural position.

watchPoints.text: Suzie Songs crosses to the rail early — if she settles unmolested in front James Ryan can control the pace entirely, and any horse failing to track her will be at a structural disadvantage for the whole race.

Ocean's Breath and L L Koulsty both break looking for prominent positions — early crowding or bumping between them could compromise their own chances and disrupt Frescobaldi's intended tracking berth just behind the leader.

Yaupon De Replay's run style only pays off if the pace is genuinely sustainable — watch the sectionals through the first three furlongs to judge whether Dylan Browne McMonagle will have enough tempo ahead of him to generate a meaningful finish.

Sir Benji's trip drop from 10f to 7f is a notable unknown — if Gavin Cromwell has specifically targeted this race for a speed test, any unexpected early dash from him could momentarily disrupt the pace picture before he inevitably drops away.
